blocks.text: Organizing your browser for creative flow

Your browser setup dictates how much time you lose to administrative friction. If your bookmarks are buried and your tabs are chaotic, you waste time every single day. Start by creating separate Chrome profiles for different clients or projects. Go to your profile icon in the top right corner and select Add. This keeps your project-specific bookmarks, history, and logins clean and separate.

Extensions are useful, but too many will slow down your machine. Only keep the ones you use daily. If you find your browser acting slow, go to Window > Task Manager to see which tab or extension is eating your memory. You can end the process there without restarting the whole browser.

You will eventually hit the dreaded Aw, Snap error. This usually happens when a page runs out of memory or has a conflict. First, try refreshing the page with ⌘ + R. If that fails, clear your cache for just that specific site. You do not need to wipe your entire history.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to manage your studio admin

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you stay focused on your art. When you are deep in a drawing session, you do not want to stop and type out a simple email or search for a reference image. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur a question. You can ask it to find a specific link or explain how to change a setting in Chrome.

Stop clicking through menus. Use these keyboard shortcuts to move faster. Use ⌘ + T for a new tab. Use ⌘ + L to jump straight to the address bar. If you have too many tabs open, ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow moves you to the next one instantly. Memorize these to keep your hands on your tablet or keyboard.

Communication is a large part of your business. If you use Gmail, create labels for your clients. This keeps your inbox from becoming a mountain of unread messages. You can also use Lazur to dictate quick replies. Press and hold fn to dictate your text. It cleans up your speech and formats it at the cursor, saving you from typing out repetitive feedback.

As a freelancer, your data is your livelihood. Block third-party cookies by default to prevent sites from tracking you across the web. Go to Settings > Privacy and security > Third-party cookies. Choose Block third-party cookies. This is a small step that adds a layer of protection to your business activity.
What to do when your browser is slow

If Chrome feels sluggish, check for updates. Chrome 158 is the current stable version for macOS. If you are on an older version of macOS, your browser might be capped. Always keep your browser updated to the latest version to ensure you have the best security patches and performance improvements.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Chrome for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can point at buttons on your screen or guide you through a process one step at a time.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on older Mac models?
faq.answer: Lazur works on macOS devices with Apple silicon or Intel chips. Ensure you are running a supported version of macOS.

faq.question: How do I clear my cache for a single site?
faq.answer: Click the lock icon in the address bar, select Site settings, and then click Clear data.

faq.question: Is my data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut key. Audio and screenshots are not stored.
